title: CALLED TO JUDGE: COMMANDED TO BE JUST

sense.text:
Moses asks, “How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?” A cumbrance is a burden, a hindrance, an obstacle, a source of trouble. Moses could not carry it alone because there were too many of them, and it is the same today: the Bishops, Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Yawasap, Bishop Kani, cannot do this alone. There are too many of us.

So what did the Bishop do? He appointed deacons, captains, officers of 90, 80, 60, 50, 20 and 10, and under them the soldiers. A soldier is not part of leadership. It is called soldier for a reason: a soldier is being prepared to become a leader, to become a judge. So a soldier takes counsel from an officer, not from another soldier, because that officer is supposed to build him up and prepare him to be an officer.

When you become an officer, you are a judge. In a courthouse nobody has more power than the judge: he can send everybody in that courthouse to jail, the lawyer and the prosecutor too. Whatever he says goes. As a judge you can destroy, and you can build. That is what you were called to be. But being called to judge, you are also commanded to be just. You cannot be a wicked judge. Some accepted the position of judge but not the command to be just, and that is how we know they do not understand what they stepped into.

Nobody walks out of law school and becomes a judge. Some wait for years before they are appointed, because the position is earned. Those positions come with heavy consequences and heavy responsibilities: to whom much is given, much is required. And old age does not mean wisdom. It just means old age. There are young men among us with more wisdom than old men, and the Most High God is not looking at your age.

“Take you wise men”: a judge must be wise. A judge cannot be a dummy; a stupid judge will destroy everything. That is why you must know the scriptures. A judge who does not know the scriptures will eventually become a traitor.

“And understanding”: a judge must have understanding, understanding of the scriptures.

“And known among your tribes”: a judge must be known. That is reputation. Before a president appoints a judge he looks at his background, his reputation, and the cases he has judged, to see if there are any flaws, because there are corrupt judges. And some of our officers are corrupt. Some who used to be officers in Liberia were corrupt. We cannot have corrupt men ruling us.

So your reputation is looked at: how you deal with your wife, how you deal with your children, how you deal with the brother sitting next to you, your reputation in the congregation. All of that is looked at before a man is appointed a judge and officer. Some have a horrible reputation, and they will not be traveling with the Deacon.

Spiritually we are all a bunch of kids. If you have been sitting here eight years, you are eight years old, no matter how much gray hair you have. This is a school of learning; we are students.

“And I will make them rulers over you.” To rule something means you have power over it. Are you ready to rule ten men? Can you even rule yourself? Can you rule your own household? A ruler cannot be emotional. Some officers feel offended at any little thing: a captain tells them to tuck their pants in their boots, or that their kids keep running around destroying things, and they want to bring that leader up on charges. That is too emotional. A judge cannot be emotional.

“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do.” “So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known”: these are the qualifications. Wise in the scriptures and in your decisions, and wise here and at home, not just here.

Known also means a good reputation at your workplace. You cannot be a judge in Israel and then be at work talking about going to the bar and the hoe who was looking at you. That means you are faking it somewhere, and more than likely you are faking it here, because your spirit agrees with what is out there. You are only a judge when you are among us. Do not think the Most High God does not see you.

“Captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” Another word for these is judges. A soldier becomes a judge of ten; a judge of ten becomes a judge of twenty, and up it goes.

An officer of ten should not be counseling with an officer of ten, if there are others in the camp. He should mentor with the man he wants to become like: the ten with the twenty, the fifties with the sixties, seventies and eighties, the nineties with the captains, because that is the next thing. Some officers of ninety are never heard from; they do not understand the ranking. Some of them were in the military and understand rank there, but in the Most High God’s military they have no idea.

Moses is saying: if you are an officer of ten, you should be able to lead ten men with no problem. That is why the word is rulers. Tell an officer of twenty to take twenty men outside and do this and that, and there should be no problem. A captain of a hundred should lead a hundred men with no problem.

Expand your mind. We just traveled all over Africa, the Caribbean, South America and Europe for Passover, and some camps have hundreds of men. Could you lead them? Those men will be looking at you to lead with full ability and confidence, for the wisdom you gained being around bishops, deacons and captains. To them you are the man the Bishop sent, the representation of the bishop, the deacons and the captains they see on video, and they will not take anything less. When they are confused by the way you move, they know something is wrong, and it comes from a lack of study: you have not really been around a bishop, and you have not built yourself up.

“And I charged your judges at that time”: after he names the officers, he calls them judges, because that is what they are.

“Saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously”: to judge righteously you must be just, not partial. Some are not just. Some are evil as hell; they want the position to destroy men, to destroy brothers. “Between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

“Ye shall not respect persons in judgment”: you cannot be partial. This is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position. It comes with heavy responsibility.

“But ye shall hear the small as well as the great”: you have to hear both sides, the small matters and the great matters.

“Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man.” You are not here to be loved or liked; you are judges, not here to make friends. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them. Some get offended when judgment falls on their friend: what the hell does that have to do with you? Mind your own damn business. At Passover there were people who were not even there who got offended at a judgment, knowing nothing of what happened, only the result. You have to be crazy to be offended about something you know nothing about. That is how we know they are Israel: we are crazy as all hell. Your fear is supposed to be toward the Most High, not toward men.

“For the judgment is God’s.” The judgment is the Most High’s.

“And the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.” The cause is any matter. When you do not know how to judge a matter, do not just wing it, because your decision can destroy somebody. There is nothing wrong with reaching out to a deacon, a captain, or an officer of higher rank and asking how they would judge it. When the time comes, a judge does not say, my bad.

In a judge’s chamber the walls are lined with books of old cases. When the judge says, I’ll be back with my decision, he goes back to those old cases, because the same kind of case may have come twenty years before. Lawyers and prosecutors build their cases on old cases. A judge is not always right; that is why records are kept, so the decision can be made the right way.

Some have a bishop, a captain, or a high-ranking officer in their camp, and they hide from them. Those men are your old records. That is why the leaders go back to the war room after class: to build you with the old records. And where are the old records? The scriptures. When you ask the Bishop a question, he never gives you his opinion. He goes to the old records, takes them, breaks them down, and makes them new to you. The prophecies are in the old records. It is said carnally, through the courthouse, so that those who do not understand the spiritual thing can understand it.

And as a judge you must understand what discerning means, and a judge must be able to travel.

precepts.why:
“Ye shall not respect persons in judgment.” James shows what respect of persons is: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.”

Respect of persons is having one man in admiration over another. It is respecting one over another, and it is also how you deal with matters between brothers when you prefer one over another, having men’s persons in admiration because of some advantage. There is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

Here is the end of it: “Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” It is about judges again, judging without respect of persons. If you hold one in admiration for the advantage you may gain, you are become judges of evil thoughts.

Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something they can gain from the person they should be judging: he gives them gifts, he is their ride to Sabbath, he got them a job. So they are partial in judgment because of what that person provides. Or they think, I’m just not going to judge because that is my friend. That is an evil, evil thing.

“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We know thou shalt not kill and thou shalt not steal like the back of our hand, but respect of persons, in judgment or in having men’s persons in admiration for advantage, is also sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God. Much is required of the judge: he must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy.

In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend’s folly, and none of us should, leader or not. Because someone is your friend you do not want to speak out or reveal the sin, and once it is revealed you do not want to be part of the judgment. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. We have to stand on what God said.

Anyone you call a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give it a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God. His Hebrew name is gone, and he goes back to Tyrone Biggins, Cleophus Jenkins, whatever it was.

sense.text:
A judge must be able to travel. Some have never gone beyond their mama’s house; born in the South, they never left the South. And that is not said to Judah only, but to Levi, Benjamin, all twelve tribes, as this last Passover showed.

“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work.” When you are raised up as an officer of ten, the Bishop is saying, separate me that brother for the work. And the work is not only in Atlanta, Miami or California. Is Israel only scattered in Atlanta, only in America? Separate them for the work means that wherever the work is, you have to go there.

“Whereunto I have called them.” It does not say the Bishop called you, or the Deacon, or the Captain. The Most High God called you for the work.

“And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.” When you became an officer you were anointed, so that the spirit of the Most High would come upon you to go and do the work, and you were sent away. So when the phone call comes for you to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you except yes. We see it. We act like we do not see you, but we have seen you, and most of all God sees you.

“So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.” Paul traveled, and so do we: this Passover the brothers were as far as Tanzania. We are continuing the Acts of the Apostles. Many hate us for it, but we do not care; we are doing the Most High God’s work. We just came from all over the world keeping Passover and bringing the good news.

precepts.why:
The work is wherever Israel is, and the prophecy says where that is: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations.” Among the nations, not just in America, not just in Florida.

“And ye shall be left few in number among the heathen.” No matter where you go, you are going to see Israelites. A captain just came back from Trinidad and Suriname for Passover, and there were the brothers with him. Separated for the work means going to all those nations where Israel was scattered.

sense.text: “Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks”: both to the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, “repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.”

“And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there.” Paul was going to Jerusalem not knowing what would happen; they might kill him. When you leave your house, you are traveling. Once you say you want to travel internationally with the brothers and are given a good report, understand there is a chance you might not come back. Always keep that in your head: the minute you forget it you let your guard down, and remembering it keeps you sharp. It is the same every Saturday you go to camp; there is a chance you might not come back.

Paul did not know what would happen, but he went anyway, because that is what he was called to do. That is what you were called to do. None of us know whether death will come in America or in South America.
“Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.”

“But none of these things move me.” Death did not move Paul. He was not afraid of death, affliction, or being locked up. He was ready to sacrifice for this truth, because he understood what he was called for and what comes with that position.

You do not have to become an officer. Stay home with the woman and the kids. But once you step into that position, know what to expect: death, prison and affliction are part of it. If you think it is about gifts, or being served food first, you are crazy and do not understand what you are in.

Liberia has been through two horrible civil wars, where women were raped; it ended about twenty-three years ago, and young men in our camp there now, 24, 25, 26 years old, went through it as kids and saw horrible things. How dare you complain? You have some damn nerve complaining. You have no idea the blessing the Most High gave you to grow up in this country. Brothers and sisters overseas do not have running water from the faucet; water drips from a pump and that is what they wash with. America has spoiled us and made us very comfortable in captivity, so that some just want to stay in Atlanta, New York or DC and be an officer, and never go wake up the people overseas. That is what you signed up for. If you do not want to do it, give back your rank and sit down as a brother, but do not fake it.

In Liberia, outside the radio station, a girl of ten or eleven was washing her little brother’s school uniform by hand in a pot on a Sunday, and when we came out she was bathing her little brothers in a bucket. Some of our brothers and sisters cannot afford deodorant; they have to choose between deodorant and food. That is not said to degrade our brothers and sisters on the continent, but to show how some here have the nerve to complain and respect nothing. Wake up every day and thank the Lord for where you are. Shut the hell up. God is sick of you complaining, and God hates a complainer. Nobody wants to hear you. Whatever your situation here, you had it better than the brothers and sisters outside of America. That is why it is good to travel: those who complain never go anywhere and never experience anything.

precepts.why:
This is exactly the point about traveling and complaining: “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things.” The traveling spoken of is not a vacation or a cruise with your wife; it is traveling to do the work of the Lord. “And he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” The man that travels will declare wisdom.

If you do not travel, you do not know anything. You are a professional student, a local prophet, and that limits your spirit’s growth. Your spirit cannot grow if you never go and deal with other spirits in different parts of the world. Christ did not call you to stay in your local school; he called you to go forth and teach all nations.

“He that hath no experience knoweth little”: then shut your mouth and do not complain. It is the brothers who never go anywhere who complain. Your complaining comes from a place of ignorance.

“But he that hath travelled is full of prudence”: full of wisdom and knowledge. When you go to these places you learn how to deal with the dignitaries and how to get around things the locals may not be able to get around. “When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express.” Wisdom gets you places, and the wisdom you carry is to be used to open new doors of utterance.

On this Passover the wisdom of Bishop Kani was something to learn from: how he dealt with local and municipal leaders, and with a riled-up man at the transit terminal who had an issue with the teaching, and quenched that spirit. It is God-given, never degrading or looking down on them. Traveling with two bishops, as with Bishop Nathanyel and Bishop Yawasap in Sierra Leone and again this Passover, and watching them, is something you cannot put a price on. Bishop Yawasap will stand in scripture for what seems like forever, because he does not want you to miss anything; it takes passion and patience to do what he does, and if you never go, you are missing out.

Some go overseas and feel they are better than the brothers and sisters there. Anyone who travels and acts better than the locals will not travel again, because he makes us look bad. You might have a little more, but that does not make you better or give you the right to look down on them. That is an evil, demonic spirit. Those are your brothers and sisters; treat them with respect, because they have the utmost respect for you, and the Most High can change your situation just like that. And talk to your wives: some went over there disrespecting the sisters, and they will not travel again. Your wife is a reflection of you, and if you knew she was like that, why did you bring her?

sense.text:
“He that openeth, and no man shutteth.” The Most High God is opening a lot of doors to IUIC, and when those doors open we must walk through them. We do not wait until the door opens to prepare ourselves; we must be prepared before it opens, so that when it opens we walk right through. That is what we have been building you up for, and why we keep telling you to build yourself up: a door may open that finds you outside of this place.

To walk through those doors you have to know the scriptures, know how to talk to people, have respect, have discipline, and be a just judge. Some do not know how to talk to people; some are very disrespectful.

A judge has to carry himself a certain way and look a certain way. Obama said he never went into the Oval Office without a suit, because that is the highest office. We are in the Most High God’s army. Do not leave the house with wrinkled pants, a purple shirt turning white, a black shirt and black pants that are not black anymore, dirty shoes. As a leader and a judge you must carry yourself a certain way. If you do not respect yourself, do not expect the man sitting next to you to respect you. Respect is not given; it is earned.

The same with the sisters: some look real good leaving the house while their kids look like they are on crack, wrinkled pants and shirt, hair undone, which shows a mother who does not care about anybody but herself. And when somebody says something, it is, he’s disrespecting my kid. Do better, because we know you can. The same with the brothers. All of this is part of being a judge.

“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” Same mind, same spirit. When we travel we must agree; all of us traveling must be in the same mind and the same spirit. Stay in the spirit. Do not go to these countries and start bugging out. You will walk in an officer and come back a member, in regular clothes. We will not allow you to leave here and go over there to destroy brothers and sisters.
“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates”: the officers are the judges, “and they shall judge the people with just judgment.” Not only judgment, but just judgment.

“One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin”: “at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.” That is, shall the matter be judged. There must be witnesses. Do not just take somebody’s word for it, even your friend’s. Negroes lie, just in case you did not know. Negroes always add to what happened so they can make themselves feel better. As a judge you cannot be like that. Two or three witnesses, and let the matter be established.
“Let the prophets speak two or three, and let the other judge.” Do not talk over each other. Wait your turn, then talk. That is how you judge matters.
“That ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you.” We all must speak the same thing, and there must be no division among us. Leaders must speak the same thing: no division.

“But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.” When we teach, we are not there to convince anybody of anything, to argue or to debate. That will not win souls. We are there to teach and plant the seed; whether they accept it is up to the Messiah.

It is nothing personal. Everybody is not going to agree with you; some will curse you out and call you names. You are there to do a job: do the job and leave. Teach the scriptures and stay in the scriptures. Keep your emotion out of the Bible and your personal opinion out of the word of God. Nobody wants to hear your opinion, and God does not care about it.

“A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.” This is how to judge matters, for the new officers. Do not argue back and forth. Reject. Once you put the law down and they do not want to hear it, bye. That is it.
“Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.” Being condemned of himself.

“Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools.” A pastor said this verse means take your shoes off before you go into the church. That is not what it is talking about.

When the Most High called Moses, he told him to take his shoes off, for where he stood was holy ground. The shoes represent all the philosophy Moses learned in Egypt. Moses grew up in the house of a Pharaoh and learned all the religion and philosophies of a people worshipping many gods, and the Most High said, do not come in here with that same mindset. So keep thy foot when you come into the house of God: do not come here with the trash you learned in the Christian churches. Whatever you learned, you have to start all over again. That is why Christ said you must come as a little child, because a little child is ready to learn; you can teach a little child anything. It is easier to raise strong children than to repair broken men, and we are a broken people.

To the sisters, especially the young virgin sisters: there is a consequence for everything you do in life, and it will come back and bite you. Men have something called ego. Every man wants to walk into a room with a woman everybody respects; no man, rich or poor, wants to walk in with a woman every man there has slept with. Based on the world, 90% of men love hoes, and 90% of men will not marry hoes. They will sleep with them; they will not marry them. Some sisters believe they can live that way all their lives and a man will still come in and say, I’ll marry you. It does not work like that. That is why the Most High put the jealousy of a man in the Proverbs. Go to school, get a degree and a job, but men do not care how successful you are or how much money you make. What men care about is respect and loyalty. A hundred master’s degrees, men don’t give a damn. If you are disrespectful, they do not care about the rest.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” Not ask the Bishop, not ask the Deacon, not ask the Captain: let him ask of God. Wisdom comes from the Most High. If you want wisdom, pray for it. That is what a leader does, and what a judge does.

The greatest judge that ever walked the earth was King Solomon, and he prayed to the Most High for wisdom. He did not ask for riches; he asked for wisdom and understanding to judge the Most High’s people, and because of that the Most High blessed him with riches too, and he became the richest man on the earth. That wisdom did not come from men, and no man can give it to you. When you judge, pray to the Most High for that wisdom, so that you may judge justly and righteously. Without it you cannot be a righteous judge or a just judge.

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.” Some have wisdom but no understanding, and what is the purpose of all that wisdom without understanding?

Here is how you know a man has no understanding: as soon as judgment comes on him, everybody hates him. He has good wisdom, he knows the scriptures, he knows precept upon precept, but as soon as he is judged he forgets every precept he knows. That is having no understanding.

sense.text:
“Walk in wisdom toward them that are without”: toward the ones who are not here. You must be an example not only here but outside. The people at your job know you are an Israelite; you have your fringes on and you talk about the Bible. Then your wicked coworker invites you to the bar down the street after work, and you go, and you come back telling the Deacon there were hoes in there. What did you expect to be in a bar?

Because you are stupid. You are simple. Some have been coming for years and are still simple, talking about sitting at the bar when they should have been preparing for the new moon. Some are too old for this: you have a wife and kids at home, and you are sitting in a bar destroying your family. When are you going to change?

“Even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.” Discerning does not come overnight. You must pray for it, over and over again. Officers were not made judges because they could already discern; they were made judges because of the potential seen in them to become great leaders who will eventually discern. Some cannot discern anything, and a leader must be able to discern. Discerning can save your life; it can save this whole room.

If you are not sure, do not make a quick decision. Ask. There is nothing wrong with telling a brother, I’ll get back to you. None of us in this room know everything, and the Bishop does not know everything. Some ask the Bishop the craziest questions, like medical questions, whether they should take a medication. What the hell? He is not a doctor; go talk to a doctor. Did the doctor prescribe it? Then take it. Some of you are crazy, and the doctor gave you that medication because you are crazy.

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age.” You cannot give a baby a big piece of chicken; he will choke. Some want to learn things before their age. Learn the simple things first. A great judge starts from the bottom, just as nobody is appointed a judge straight out of school; it takes time to build yourself up. Start with Deuteronomy 28 and learn it. A young man once said nobody could teach him anything out of the Bible anymore, and when asked to break down Deuteronomy 28, he could not. This is a big book, and it will take us a lifetime to learn it.

Stay away from big things that have nothing to do with you. The kingdom is not based on how many scriptures or how many deep prophecies you know. It is based on keeping the laws and doing what the book says. If you are not doing what the book says, the deep things will not help you. You cannot do the simple thing, you go without your fringes, but you want to know the deep things. That makes no sense. That is why it speaks of the strong meat: to discern both good and evil.

Leadership is not a rank to be achieved; it is a responsibility, and the responsibility is to see the men around you rise, to build them up. If you are a judge, do not keep the men around you down. Build them up, if they want to be built up. Never force a man to do the work; he must do it willingly, because when you force him the spirit is not there. The men traveling around the world are put together in teams for nearly impossible tasks: meetings with dignitaries, school seminars, radio and TV shows. That takes a certain caliber of man. A man who was forced to come around was only in the room; when you have to rely on him in a life-or-death situation, you find out he bugs out, or that the spirit is not on him. You must know the men you labor among.

The leader is responsible for the people who are responsible for the people who are responsible for the results. That is the ranking system. A task is given to the captain, the captain gives it to the officers under him, and down it goes; and if it never gets done, it is the captain who is looked at, not the men at the bottom. It is not easy, and the Bishop always says Black people do not work well together; we need to learn to. It can be done with the spirit of the Most High. At one Passover overseas, an officer put in charge of the lamb was talking about serving it with rice and beans in the school. You have to know these things as a judge, and that is why you must use the bishops, deacons and captains in your camp: the men over there will be looking to you to show them how.

If every Passover comes and nobody under you is rising, from brother to soldier, from soldier to officer, that shows poor leadership. On the other side of the world the brothers were very bashful and spoke very low; when they were put up to teach and speak publicly, with authority, one brother became a whole new man. You are supposed to raise men up to stand in your stead. If something happens to the officer of a school and nobody has been built up, that school will fall.

You do not have to like everybody, or get along with everybody. The job is to lead everybody without letting your bias, your opinion or your emotions into it; to respect every single person, and to grow every single person, so that each one also becomes a judge. The job is not to be liked.

To prove it: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

“Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat.” There is nothing in that scripture that says you were sent to be liked. That is not the job and not the mission. You were sent to wake up the people, to tell the people how evil they are, that they must repent and come back to the Messiah. Some want rank for the wrong reason; they forgot the mission and forgot the job.
“And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.”

“Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace.” The Lord came to Paul in a vision and strengthened him not to be afraid, but to speak. When you travel to these places, because of the influx of a certain religion, of the heathen, you may feel discouraged and think the mission will not prosper. That is not why the Lord sent you there. He sent you to do as he commanded.

That is why getting built up before going is so important. Going into other lands, you learn from men who have already been to similar regions and can give you the strategies of war. We are at war, whether you know it or not, and a war has been waged against you since the day you were in the womb. They say the most dangerous place for a Black child is its mother’s womb; they push abortion in our communities. When you were little and heard all the jingle bell songs in the store, they were warring with you. So the Lord strengthened Paul, because there was a mission he was sending him on.

“For I am with thee.” As dangerous as many of the places we go to are, the Lord is with us. “And no man shall set on thee to hurt thee”: no man will hurt you to the point that the mission is hindered.

“For I have much people in this city.” We go to places we have never touched down before: Zanzibar, Madagascar, a place known only from a cartoon. Seeing the brothers marching through Madagascar strengthened us. The Lord used them to strengthen us, as brothers go into lands we only thought were stories in books, and they are real places.

“And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.” The Lord strengthened him, and he did not hold back: he taught the commandments of God and he taught Christ. That is where we are going. The next mission will not be two weeks or four weeks; the bar is raised for every leader. The diaspora is scattered to the four corners of the earth, and who is going to raise them up? We did not come here just for a Sabbath sandwich. There are regions not yet visited, and places with a congregation but no established sanctuary, that need brothers to go there and teach. We are reading and living the Acts of the Apostles.

“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul did not stop at Corinth; he went on to Ephesus, and over all the country of Galatia, to strengthen the disciples. The Lord told him in Corinth not to be afraid, for he had much people in that city. We go to these strange lands with all confidence that God’s people are there. The Lord did not send us into a barren land not occupied by the children of Israel.

Look at the faces of the children at the school in Tanzania, lined up: those are the children of Israel. Camps that say Israelites are only in America are crazy as hell. Tanzania and Zanzibar are 99% Muslim. They had never heard that Jesus Christ was Black, that the Israelites are Black, or that we should keep the commandments of God, and now those children are asking where they can go to hear more. They want to be strengthened by the word of God. That is the men going all over the world to where Christ has never been taught.

The key is strengthening the disciples. If you are not about strengthening the disciples, and you are out of order trying to move someplace else, to another country, it is not going to work. You are not about the mission; you have ulterior motives.

precepts.why:
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” Paul went over the country “in order”. Some brothers and sisters just up and move to a strange land all of a sudden. They are not building up the men, they are not built up themselves, and it causes confusion.

Do not use Acts 18 to say, I went to build up the men in a strange land like the scripture said. You are out of order, and it will not be tolerated; you may lose your rank and have to sit down. When you visit another camp, a travel request is made. From now on, anyone who moves to these countries without proper protocol will not fellowship with IUIC; they are on their own. If you show up saying you are with IUIC in some state, and no phone call came from that school, you cannot come in. That is an agent move, and some are agents. IUIC is about order. We know Black people hate order, and that is why a lot of them hate IUIC anyway. Stay the hell out of our school. Go anywhere without doing it the right way, and you stay out.

sense.text:
“But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God”: that is the carnal man, the evil man. “For they are foolishness unto him”: he cannot understand the spiritual things or these scriptures. He has no understanding and no wisdom, and he cannot be a judge. “Neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.”

Joined to strengthening the disciples: you should see the joy on the faces of the brothers and sisters in these countries when they see us. It is not money they want. They have watched the Bishop, the deacons and the captains on video for years, thousands of miles away, thinking we do not even know they are there. Then these men show up in their school, sit at the same table, eat with them, joke with them, answer their questions, and the sisters sit in circles with Mother Shamaya, whom they have looked up to. One sister cried nonstop and said the Most High kept her alive just to see the Bishop. What they want is for you to open the scriptures and strengthen them with the Bible: to let them know it is going to be okay, that they are not in this alone, that you will not turn your back on them when you leave. That is the only assurance they want. These are things we take for granted.

Our school in Liberia loses power almost every two hours, and it is hot. They need a commercial generator, air conditioning, toilet tissue, paper towels and water, and we cannot just tell them, I’m going to pray for you. In Tanzania fringes are so expensive, sold as material for rich people’s furniture, that the donated fringes brought great joy. The giving through the booster club goes further than you can imagine; everybody was able to celebrate Passover, with decoration and lamb, because of it. We are only weak when we are alone. When we unify, nothing can break us.

“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault”: a man commits a sin. “Ye which are spiritual”: you who are a righteous judge, a just judge, “restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.”

It does not say how long, when judgment comes and a brother is put out. Every case is not the same, and you have to treat every case as it comes, because every man does not have the same spirit. Six months out may be fine for one man and destroy another. Be very careful not to destroy them.

“Considering thyself”: if you put that man out for a year, and a couple of years later you commit the same sin, would you want to be cut off for a year? Once you pass judgment, consider yourself. It is not about get out, get out. None of us in this commission is perfect; the righteous fall seven times and get back up again, and we will make mistakes. When a brother stands before you as a judge, consider the judgment before you pass it: if it were you, would you want that same judgment?

“Lest thou also be tempted.” Lest the same thing happen to you, and now you want mercy, when you had no mercy on that brother.

The protocol when a brother is put out is not simply no communication. An officer is assigned over the man. The man who was put out reports to that officer, keeps him updated, watches the classes and gives his notes, and the officer follows up with leadership on how he is doing. If you put him out with no contact and no communication, how could you restore him? That is how he is restored: he keeps contact with the man appointed over him, and that man gives the report. The man who messed up calls the officer; the deacon does not call him. He has to fix what he messed up, and there must be godly sorrow.
“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” Why say that? Because you might find yourself doing the same thing that brother did. Be very careful.

“Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you.” Many forget this scripture when they step into the position of a judge. Of everything said about how to be a judge and judge rightly: when you step into that office, travel to all these countries, work with the people and open their eyes, taking them out of the grip of Satan, what did you think would happen to you? Satan will come for you, and when he does you had better be prepared. Some are just happy: I’m an officer now, I can tell men what to do, I can travel, I eat first. “That he may sift you as wheat.”

“But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.” Our job is to pray for each other that our faith fail not. Pray for the leaders, and pray for the men traveling to these countries: they go to new territories and lands they have never been, and they do not know what is waiting for them. Never think Satan is not going to come for you. This is not a walk in the park; you will not just walk in and get the kingdom. Jacob’s trouble is coming, and it is only going to get worse. Our job is to strengthen each other, here and abroad, support each other, and pray for each other.

“Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth”: if you commit a fault, if you fall, if you find yourself committing a sin. “And one convert him”: convert means change. One helps him get better, helps him to change.

“Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.” He that helps that brother, that sinner, turn from the error of his ways is saving that soul from death.

We have a big job, and we pray the Most High God sends more laborers. Everyone should be able to get up and travel, but you have to get your mind right and build yourself first. The Most High God is opening a lot of doors to IUIC. When you go to those places, those people are one of you, and you are one of them; the sisters there are one of you. You are there to build them and strengthen them. They look up to you and have the greatest respect for you, so do not disappoint them, and show them the same respect. These people love us, and some say they wish we did not have to leave. We are lions.
